_meta.description: Critical-minerals coverage. Shows which officially designated minerals this universe actually gives exposure to, and — more importantly — which it does not.

us.name: US critical minerals list (USGS, 2022 final)
us.note: 50 minerals. Copper, potash, silicon, silver and lead appeared in the 2025 DRAFT revision but the 2022 list is the last one finalised. Uranium is excluded as a 'fuel mineral' by statute, not because it is unimportant.

eu.name: EU Critical Raw Materials Act (Reg. 2024/1252)
eu.note: 34 critical raw materials, of which 17 are designated STRATEGIC with 2030 capacity benchmarks.

cn.name: China export-control / restricted list
cn.note: Inverse signal: what China restricts is what China dominates. Cumulative through the 2025 REE expansion. Dates given per mineral.

_meta.caveat: Designations are transcribed from the cited list versions. Where a mineral's status changed in a draft or unpublished revision it is noted in the entry rather than silently updated. Verify before relying on any single flag.

exposure_scale.primary: A holding whose main business is producing or separating this mineral.
exposure_scale.processing: A holding that refines, converts or separates it but does not mine it.
exposure_scale.byproduct: Exposure only as a secondary output — supply cannot respond to this mineral's price alone.
exposure_scale.enduse: A holding that consumes it. Not supply exposure.

_meta.controllers_note: Who actually controls supply, separately from what we own. A listed Chinese producer is investable via Stock Connect and is marked 'listed in China'; a state entity is marked as not investable. Conflating the two understates how much of the chokepoint is actually purchasable.
_meta.byproduct_note: Where a mineral is a byproduct, the main suppliers are named together with what actually pays their bills. This is the mechanism behind the chokepoint: a producer whose revenue is 99% aluminium will not expand output because gallium tripled.

minerals.name: Bismuth
minerals.why: Non-toxic lead replacement; a lead/copper byproduct under Chinese control since Feb 2025.

byproduct_of.note: Bismuth is a lead/copper smelting byproduct. 5N Plus (VNP.TO) and AMG (AMG.AS) process it; the upstream is Chinese lead smelters whose PRIMARY REVENUE IS LEAD AND ZINC.

minerals.name: Graphite
minerals.why: Every lithium-ion anode. China controls the overwhelming majority of spherical and synthetic anode-grade supply, and put it under export licensing in Dec 2023.

controllers.name: BTR New Material
controllers.note: Largest anode-material maker globally; not resolving on Yahoo.

controllers.name: Shanshan / Putailai
controllers.note: Chinese anode majors control the overwhelming majority of spherical and synthetic graphite.

minerals.name: Gallium
minerals.why: GaN power electronics and RF. China put it under export licensing in Aug 2023; there is no meaningful Western primary production because it is an aluminium byproduct.

byproduct_of.note: Gallium is extracted from the Bayer-process liquor at alumina refineries. Chalco (2600.HK) is the practical global source and Alcoa (AA) the Western one — but for both, PRIMARY REVENUE IS ALUMINIUM. Gallium is a trace stream worth a rounding error to them, so a higher gallium price does not make them produce more aluminium.

minerals.name: Germanium
minerals.why: Infrared optics, fibre and space solar. Same Aug 2023 Chinese controls; a zinc byproduct, so supply cannot respond to price independently.

byproduct_of.note: Germanium is recovered from zinc concentrate residues. Nexa (NEXA) and Korea Zinc are real sources, and 5N Plus (VNP.TO) purifies it — but PRIMARY REVENUE IS ZINC for the miners and a broad specialty-materials mix for 5N Plus. Germanium supply therefore tracks the zinc cycle, not germanium demand.

minerals.name: Tungsten
minerals.why: Hardest metal in industrial use — armour, penetrators, cutting tools. China put it under export control in Feb 2025.

controllers.name: Xiamen Tungsten
controllers.note: China's largest tungsten producer; China holds the overwhelming majority of supply and put it under export control in Feb 2025.

minerals.name: Scandium
minerals.why: Aluminium-scandium alloys. Tiny market, almost entirely byproduct, under Chinese HREE licensing since 2025.

byproduct_of.note: Scandium is recovered from other operations' waste streams. NioCorp (NB) would produce it at Elk Creek alongside niobium, but PRIMARY REVENUE THERE IS NIOBIUM. No scandium-primary mine operates anywhere.

minerals.name: Antimony
minerals.why: Flame retardants, ammunition primers, photovoltaic glass clarifier. China banned/licensed exports Sep 2024 and the price repriced permanently.

controllers.name: Hunan Gold / Chinese producers
controllers.note: China holds roughly half of global antimony supply and banned exports in Sep 2024.

minerals.name: Hafnium
minerals.why: Control rods and superalloys; a zirconium byproduct.

byproduct_of.note: Hafnium is separated from zirconium during nuclear-grade Zr production. The suppliers are Framatome, Westinghouse and ATI (ATI) — PRIMARY REVENUE IS ZIRCONIUM CLADDING AND SPECIALTY ALLOYS. Hafnium volume is a few hundred tonnes a year globally.

minerals.name: Magnesium
minerals.why: Lightweighting alloys and aluminium alloying. China dominates primary production to an extreme degree.

controllers.name: Chinese primary producers
controllers.note: China produces the overwhelming majority of primary magnesium; no listed Western vehicle of scale exists.

minerals.name: Barite
minerals.why: Drilling mud weighting agent — unglamorous and genuinely hard to substitute.

controllers.name: Chinese and Indian producers
controllers.note: Barite supply is concentrated in China, India and Morocco.

minerals.name: Tellurium
minerals.why: CdTe thin-film solar; a copper-refining byproduct.

byproduct_of.note: Tellurium comes from copper anode slimes. Freeport (FCX) and Rio Tinto's Kennecott are genuine sources with PRIMARY REVENUE FROM COPPER; 5N Plus (VNP.TO) refines it to solar grade. No producer would expand copper output for tellurium.

minerals.name: Indium
minerals.why: ITO for displays and touchscreens; a zinc byproduct.

byproduct_of.note: Same host ore as germanium. Nexa (NEXA) and Korea Zinc again, with PRIMARY REVENUE FROM ZINC. Indium is a residue stream.

minerals.name: Tantalum
minerals.why: Capacitors. Conflict-mineral supply chain, heavily DRC/Rwanda.

minerals.name: Vanadium
minerals.why: Steel strengthening and vanadium redox flow batteries for long-duration storage.

minerals.name: Fluorspar
minerals.why: Hydrofluoric acid feeds refrigerants, fluoropolymers and the LiPF6 battery electrolyte.

controllers.name: Chinese producers
controllers.note: China is the largest fluorspar producer; Orbia's Mexican mine is the main non-Chinese alternative.

minerals.name: Cobalt
minerals.why: Cathode stability. Mined overwhelmingly in the DRC, refined overwhelmingly in China.

controllers.name: CMOC Group
controllers.note: Now the world's largest cobalt producer via TFM and KFM in the DRC — it overtook Glencore.

controllers.name: Huayou Cobalt
controllers.note: Dominant cobalt refiner; the refining step is more concentrated than the mining.

minerals.name: Nickel
minerals.why: High-nickel cathodes and stainless. Class 1 battery-grade supply is far tighter than headline nickel.

minerals.name: Manganese
minerals.why: Battery-grade high-purity manganese sulphate is a separate, far more concentrated market than the ore.

minerals.name: Niobium
minerals.why: Microalloying steel. Effectively a single-country, near-single-company supply from Brazil.

minerals.name: Rare earths (Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb)
minerals.why: Permanent magnets for EV traction motors, wind turbines, missile guidance and every robot joint. China separates the overwhelming majority, and heavy REE separation outside China is close to zero.

controllers.name: China Northern Rare Earth
controllers.note: Roughly half of Chinese light-REE quota; the single largest producer on earth.

controllers.name: Shenghe Resources
controllers.note: REE trading and processing; historically an MP Materials offtake partner.

minerals.name: Lithium
minerals.why: Battery cathode and electrolyte. Mining is diversified; conversion to battery-grade chemical is not.

controllers.name: Ganfeng Lithium
controllers.note: Largest lithium chemical converter; conversion is far more concentrated than mining.

minerals.name: Titanium
minerals.why: Aerospace structures. Sponge and mill-product capacity outside Russia and China is the bottleneck, not the ore.

minerals.name: Beryllium
minerals.why: Defence-critical with essentially zero Western substitute; one integrated Western producer.

minerals.name: Platinum group (Pt, Pd, Rh, Ir, Ru)
minerals.why: Autocatalysts, hydrogen electrolysers and fuel cells. Iridium and ruthenium are tiny, opaque markets with acute single-country concentration.

minerals.name: Helium
minerals.why: Semiconductor fabs, MRI and cryogenics. Cannot be synthesised; a natural-gas byproduct.

minerals.name: Boron
minerals.why: Borates for glass, agriculture and permanent-magnet grain refining; near-duopoly supply.

controllers.name: Eti Maden
controllers.note: Turkish state monopoly holding the majority of world borate reserves — not investable.

controllers.name: Rio Tinto
controllers.note: US Borax at Boron, California — the main non-Turkish source.

minerals.name: Chromium
minerals.why: Stainless steel; South Africa and Kazakhstan dominate.

minerals.name: Silicon metal
minerals.why: Polysilicon, semiconductors and silicones. Energy-intensive smelting concentrated in China and Norway.

minerals.name: Aluminium / bauxite
minerals.why: Conductor, lightweighting and packaging. Smelting is an electricity arbitrage as much as a mining business.

controllers.name: Chalco / Aluminum Corp of China
controllers.note: Bauxite through aluminium; also the practical source of gallium.

minerals.name: Zirconium
minerals.why: Nuclear fuel cladding — hafnium-free zirconium is a specialised, concentrated supply chain.

minerals.name: Zinc
minerals.why: Galvanising — and the host ore for germanium and indium, so it gates two semiconductor materials.

byproduct_of.note: Zinc is mined for itself, but it is the host for germanium and indium — so zinc economics gate two semiconductor materials.

minerals.name: Copper
minerals.why: The universal conductor. No substitute at scale; 16-17 year permitting in democracies.

controllers.name: Zijin Mining
controllers.note: One of the fastest-growing copper producers globally.

minerals.name: Tin
minerals.why: Solder. Every chip package and PCB joint; 3D chiplet stacking increases joints per chip.

minerals.name: Phosphate
minerals.why: Fertiliser and LFP cathode. Non-renewable and geographically extreme — Morocco holds most of the world's reserves.

minerals.name: Uranium
minerals.why: Reactor fuel. Excluded from the US critical list by statute as a fuel mineral, which is a legal artefact rather than a judgment on criticality.

minerals.name: Silver
minerals.why: Solar cells and electrical contacts — the only precious metal with a large, growing industrial demand leg.

minerals.name: Gold
minerals.why: Monetary hedge and central-bank reserve asset rather than an industrial input.

minerals.name: Potash
minerals.why: Fertiliser. Concentrated in Canada, Russia and Belarus.
